framework-proposal-and-test: Abstract, p.1: the authors state what they propose and that the framework is tested under a pre-specified benchmark; read in context with Sec. 1 and Sec. 5-6, which describe that protocol
version-2-supersedes-v1: Abstract Version note, p.1: states what v2 supersedes, carries forward and adds; Sec. 4.1 and Table 2 confirm the registry of changes
prespecification-before-analysis: Sec. 1, p.4: the authors' stated protocol; Sec. 5 and Sec. 6.7 repeat it. It is the authors' own account of their process, graded as stated setup
data-complexity-definition: Sec. 3, p.6: 'We define data complexity as...', the paper's own definition
interaction-complexity-definition: Sec. 3.1.3, p.7: defined by the cumulant threshold rule (Eq. 2 and the display); the same paragraph says it is representation and estimator dependent
expressibility-definition: Sec. 3.2.3, p.10: expressibility is defined as the KL divergence of the circuit's state distribution from the Haar distribution; Sec. 4.4 uses the same definition. The value says no more than this
nine-component-complexity-vector: Table 1, p.7 lists nine components (H, dpca, d2nn, I2, Ih, K, M, R, T); the caption states each is rank-normalized by Eq. (6)
rank-normalization-definition: Sec. 4.2, p.14, Eq. (6): v_i(D) is the fraction of benchmark datasets with f_i no larger than f_i(D); the CDF is frozen and new datasets are interpolated. Sec. 6.4-6.5 refit the ranks on outer-training datasets per fold, which does not contradict the definition
quantum-composite-ensembles: Sec. 4.2, p.15: ten ensembles (five reference, five parity probes w in {1,2,4,6,8}), equal weights, n = 8, N = 256, labelled exploratory
quantum-composite-not-tested-as-predicto: Sec. 4.2, p.16: the authors state that the composite is evaluated, not tested as a predictor, and give the reason. A limit on their own exploratory analysis
curvature-pillar-not-implemented: Sec. 4.2 scope note, p.16: specified but not implemented; every dataset is non-graph; v5 dropped; H2 reduces to topology alone. Repeated in Sec. 8.4
v-q-split-definition: Sec. 4.2, p.16: induced complexity is a property of the dataset-embedding pair; v(D) is embedding-free and q(D, phi) is defined separately (Eq. 10)
corrected-scaling-form-separates-baselin: Sec. 4.3, p.17, Eq. (12): the paper's own proposed form; v to 0 gives A exp(-alpha n d) by direct substitution; H1 is stated to test it
budget-matched-edge-noiseless-simulation: Sec. 4.5, p.18, Eq. (18) and Sec. 6.3, Eq. (21): noiseless simulation with a frozen reference two-qubit error rate 1e-3 and F = (1 - eps2)^n2q
three-edge-versions-primary-target: Sec. 4.5, p.18: three edge versions defined; the primary target is e-budget. Sec. 6.3 repeats it
budget-matched-edge-not-hardware-estimat: Sec. 6.3, p.22: the budget-matched edge is stated to be a matched comparison target, not an estimate of performance on a particular platform
data-access-mode-s: Sec. 4.5, p.19: Mode S defined in the paper's bullet list
data-access-mode-q: Sec. 4.5, p.19: Mode Q defined in the paper's bullet list
data-access-mode-n: Sec. 4.5, p.19: Mode N defined in the paper's bullet list
mode-q-comparator-rule: Sec. 4.5, p.19: the comparator rule and the retention rule are stated as the framework's own adopted rules ('Under this framework'), with the dequantization papers [28, 104] cited only as motivation
encoding-cost-model-terms: Sec. 4.5, p.18, Eq. (17): the cost C_phi is defined with D_phi, W_phi and eps_phi as the value says
h5-decision-rule: Sec. 5, p.20: H5 support rule R2 >= 0.4 and ECE <= 0.1 under LODO; same in Table 6 and Eq. (31)
h1-decision-rule: Sec. 5, p.20: H1 support rule stated as in the value; same in Table 6
h2-decision-rule: Sec. 5, p.19-20: the pre-specified criterion Delta AIC >= 10; the same section says the H2 result was later withdrawn, which the value does not contradict because it states only the pre-specified rule
hypothesis-outcome-categories: Sec. 5, p.21: the four outcome categories are listed as the paper's own reporting scheme
benchmark-grid-and-cells: Sec. 6.1, p.21, Eq. (20): 27 x 10 x 6 x 5 = 8100 cells, all completed; Sec. 6.5 gives the LODO design
encoding-and-ansatz-families: Sec. 6.1, p.21: eight qubits, four encoding families, three circuit families at L in {1, 3}
seed-randomization: Sec. 6.2, p.22: the four randomized components are listed
predictor-architecture: Sec. 6.4, p.23: SVGPMultiHead with 256 inducing points and LMC over two heads; gradient boosting trained in parallel on the same representation and partitions
lodo-validation-scheme: Sec. 6.5, p.23: 27 folds, 26 training datasets, rank transform fitted on outer-training datasets only
primary-classical-comparator-lr: Sec. 6.6, p.24, Eq. (32): the primary comparator is logistic regression on the original features; its accuracy is the pre-specified reference
six-model-classical-library: Sec. 6.6, p.24: the six-model list with the stated hyperparameters (the value omits the MLP alpha, which does not change it)
classical-baselines-trained-on-raw-featu: Sec. 6.6, p.24: stated as the primary comparison. Note that Sec. 7.3 (p.29) states a fairness rule that the baseline should be evaluated on the encoded representation; the value is graded on Sec. 6.6, which describes what was run
best-of-six-is-modest-comparator: Sec. 7.2, p.26: the library is fixed rather than tuned and is stated to be a deliberately modest comparator, not the strongest classical performance. Sec. 8.3 repeats it
encoder-argument-scope-condition: Sec. 7.3, p.29: the paper states the scope condition and its failure cases in the same paragraph; the quote gives the first half and the next sentence the second half
lda-excluded-on-principle: Sec. 7.3, p.30: states which reducer the paper excludes and why; this is the paper's own design choice. The rationale about LDA is the authors' reasoning, not a result
null-is-conditional-on-regime: Sec. 7.5, p.32: the null is stated not to show that data complexity can never predict advantage, only that the present quantities do not in this regime. A limit on its own measured result
width-scaling-arm-design: Sec. 7.6, p.32: widths, nine-dataset subset, five seeds, 12,960 cells (9 x 6 x 5 x 8 x 6), stated to test a functional form and not a pre-specified hypothesis
width-arm-protocol-n4-6-10: Sec. 7.8, p.34: widths 4, 6, 10; eight non-reuploading encodings; 6,480 added cells (3 x 2160, Table 14); stated to be exploratory because collected after the fixed-width result
representation-not-shown-irrelevant: Sec. 7.8, p.34-35: the authors state the width result does not license the stronger reading and give the narrower defensible statement
h3-secondary-criterion-not-evaluated: Sec. 7.9, p.35: the authors state the Spearman criterion could not be computed because outputs were not serialized and call it an instrumentation failure, not a null result
h4-untested: Sec. 7.10, p.35: H4 is stated to be untested because it is downstream of H5; the conflation reason is in the next paragraph
h6-not-evaluable-no-mode-q: Sec. 7.11, p.35-36: no Mode-Q cells, so H6 is a boundary condition and not an empirical result; same in Sec. 4.5 and Sec. 5
shadow-hard-parity-probe-design: Sec. 7.12, p.36: the construction and the comparator (best of the six models on k <= 2 shadow features) are stated
parity-control-not-a-separation-result: Sec. 7.12, p.36: the authors state the control is not a separation result, list what the classical side was not given, and make no persistence claim
no-classical-tuning-study: Sec. 8.3, p.40: the six-model comparison is stated to be a fixed-library sensitivity analysis, not a tuned frontier, and no tuning study was run
n27-limits-effect-size-precision: Sec. 8.4, p.40: the paper states that N = 27 limits effect-size precision and says what can and cannot be concluded
circuit-regime-simulated-noiseless-n8: Sec. 8.4, p.41: pre-specified circuits n = 8, simulated, noiseless; behaviour above n = 14 and hardware noise untested. The quotes carry both sentences
postprocessing-layer-not-audited: Sec. 8.4, p.41: the authors state they have not audited the postprocessing layer with the same care and do not claim to have
encoding-ansatz-libraries-finite: Sec. 8.4, p.41: finite libraries; re-uploading encodings excluded from H1/H2 because no fixed encoded state exists to compute q on
two-tracks-parallel-not-unified: Sec. 8.4, p.41: the quantum-native control is a positive control, not a selector input; the quote carries the whole claim
target-is-competitive-rival-only: Sec. 8.4, p.41: the predictand presumes the two methods are rivals; the result is stated to be a null for this target in this cell
interaction-half-untested: Sec. 8.4, p.41-42: q(D, phi) is reported as untested rather than unsupported, with the reason (axis pinned) and the requirement for future designs
topology-and-higher-order-mi-instrument-: Sec. 8.4, p.42: instrument limitations the authors state about their own components (relative rankings, brittle at k >= 3)
corrected-estimator-global-diameter-limi: Sec. 8.4, p.42 and App. B.3: the authors state the limit of the corrected estimator and that they took the trade deliberately
scope-single-algorithm-family-mode-s: Sec. 8.5, p.42: the null is stated to apply only to this Mode-S variational-classification comparison; the algorithm family and task type are described in the same section
conclusion-not-universal-absence: Sec. 9, p.44: the paper states the result rejects the central predictive claim in the tested regime and does not establish a universal absence of advantage
conclusion-claim-is-conditional: Sec. 9, p.44: the conditions (one algorithm family, one access mode, simulated circuits up to 14 qubits) are the paper's own statement of its scope
grey-zone-tested-scope-no-theorem: Sec. 9, p.44 'In the grey zone': the tested scope, the statement that this is not evidence QML cannot work, and 'we have no theorem that forbids it' are the authors' own stated limits. The clause 'found no advantage' restates the paper's null inside that scope
suite-not-population-claim: Sec. 9, p.44-45: the 27 datasets support only a test within this suite; the suite is not a probability sample
pere-2025-data-and-code-availability: Data and code availability, p.45: repository, release statement, exact state-vector simulation in numpy, no hardware
ai-assistance-statement: AI statement, p.61: the paper's own statement of how the work was produced; the quote carries the first sentence and the next two carry the rest of the value
appendix-a-v1-reproduced-not-asserted: App. A intro, p.45: reproduces v1 unchanged; 'Nothing here is asserted by this version'; status of each element in Table 2
figures-5-6-schematic-only: App. A.2.3 and A.3.4, p.51 and p.54: both captions say the figure is schematic and illustrative only, with quantitative validation to follow in Part II (v1 text, reproduced). The figures carry no measured data
corrected-topology-estimator-spec: App. B.2, p.57: ripser, untruncated Rips, H0 excluded, bars divided by diameter, 250-point subsample with fixed seed
topology-limit-of-diameter-normalization: App. B.3, p.57-58: 'A limitation of the correction' paragraph states the limit and the local-scale trade-off; the authors took it deliberately
topology-audit-scope: App. B.4, p.60, last paragraph: the audit does not establish robustness to every estimator or representation; within the tested alternatives no stable topology contribution is found. The scope sentence is the paper's stated limit
tested-regime-scope: Sec. 9, p.44: the conditions are the paper's own statement of the scope of its claim; confirmed in context. Same passage as conclusion-claim-is-conditional

theory_low.barren-plateau-v1-data-free-limit-flaw: The limit C-tilde to 0 giving Var to 1 is read off v1's own formula, but the claim that this contradicts the Haar-random result rests on McClean et al. [69], a cited result with no derivation in this paper. Sec. 4.3, p.17
theory_low.proposition-1-attribution-decomposition: Sec. 7.3, p.29-30, Eq. (37): the identity is trivially true (the paper says it adds and subtracts A(C o P)), but the paper itself says its content is 'the attribution it forces', and that part (only the residual can be evidence of quantum advantage) is argued in one informal sentence, not proved. The value includes that claim. A narrower value that states only the identity could be graded HIGH on proved result
theory_low.corollary-1-gap-upper-bounds: Sec. 7.3, p.30: a corollary stated without proof. 'Upper-bounds rather than measures' needs the preprocessing-attributable term to be non-negative, which the text does not state or prove. The exhaustiveness claim is the identity restated
theory_low.proposition-2-encoding-cannot-create-lab: textbook, stated not proved (F129): Eq. (38) is the data-processing inequality, and the paper's only argument is 'by the data-processing inequality, which holds in the quantum case as well because E is a channel on X and Y is untouched'. Sec. 7.3, p.30. No derivation is given. The team lead decides this class
